decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Evaluated at his request; cut RM_FE_FirebreakLine. It adds nothing a vanilla floor does not: the burn line's front (IgniteLine), the smoulder relight (TryReseedStandingBurn) and the fire-hawk drop all light cells through vanilla FireUtility.ChanceToStartFireIn, so any non-flammable plant-free floor (flagstone, stone tile, concrete) stops them exactly as the firebreak does, and scorch-fruit already refuses every non-Pyrelands ground (IsScorchableGround allowlist). Its only differences are a chemfuel cost he rejected and a Firefoam research gate. Player fire defence is vanilla: pave a strip at least two cells wide (vanilla fire's far-spread jump can cross a single cell), or keep a strip cut by hand. No mod-owned plant-clearing zone is added (ember grass regrows within a week, so paving is the durable answer). Owed: excise Firebreak.xml, the kernel's FirebreakDefName special case, and switch validation.py/human_review.py fire-hygiene pads to a vanilla floor. The firefoam sprayer is untouched (its scope was not opened). He can undo this.
decisions.undo: say "keep the firebreak" and it returns as a vanilla-priced floor with no chemfuel

root_draft.text: The Pyrelands are a grass savanna that has burned for millennia and is burning still. Almost all the ground is deep ash, quite fertile wherever water reaches it, carpeted thick in ember grass that burns black and is largely green again within about a week, while free-flying ash blows across it like snow. A line of grass fire walks the map and never fully goes out.
